questions.prompt: A card is exposed during the deal. You should…

choices.text: Let the dealer apply the room's misdeal or exposed-card rule.
Ignore it and continue if you like your hand.
Show your cards so the rule is fair.

questions.explanation: Misdeals and exposed cards are procedural. Do not self-deal.

questions.prompt: You believe the dealer awarded the pot wrong. The next step is…

choices.text: Take the chips and sort it out later.
Ask the dealer for a ruling, then the floor if it is still disputed.
Accuse the other player of collusion immediately.
Post the hand on social media from the table.

questions.explanation: Keep the dispute calm and inside the room's chain: dealer, then floor.

choices.text: Keeping cards and chips clearly on the felt in front of you.
Holding the deck for the dealer.

questions.explanation: Lap cards, hidden cards, and chips off the felt cause fouled-hand and angle problems.

questions.prompt: Phones at the table are often restricted because…

choices.text: They can hide outside help or record other players' cards.

questions.explanation: Follow the room rule. Do not relay live hands to anyone off the table.
